title: The Real Reason Jet Lag Makes You Feel So Awful
hook: Jet lag does not just make you tired; it disrupts your gut.

narration.text: Jet lag does not just make you tired; it disrupts your gut.
Your body has an internal clock, the circadian rhythm, which controls many functions.
This rhythm usually aligns with the sun's cycle in your local time zone.
When you fly across time zones, your body's clock stays on its old schedule.
This mismatch between your internal clock and the local time causes jet lag.
It affects sleep, digestion, and even your concentration levels.
You might feel groggy, irritable, and have trouble sleeping at night.
What is the worst jet lag experience you have ever had?

description: Jet lag is more than just feeling tired after a long flight. It is a fundamental disruption of your body's internal clock, known as the circadian rhythm. This can impact everything from your sleep schedule to your digestion and mood.
topic: Why jet lag affects your body and mind, explaining circadian rhythm disruption.
